en: Prosperity!
Salutations to the form of Śrī Sadāśiva.
[The Beginning of the Hari-Hara Tāratamya:
Having perpetually prostrated before the elders who are experts in the specific meanings of the Śruti, Smṛti, and Purāṇas, and who are skilled with fearless intellect;
Though I have taken refuge in the non-dual One, my mind still clings to the perception of difference; therefore, I ask about the gradation of excellence among Hari, Hara, and Hiraṇyagarbha.
One lies upon the waters of the ocean beneath a banyan leaf, while the other has the ocean as his quiver during the destruction of Tripura.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 2 ||
Dwelling in mountain caves.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 6 ||
One remained after worshipping him with a thousand lotuses, while the other rejoiced together with those he had accumulated.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 7 ||
"One has a body as dark and dense as deep gloom; the other has a body as pure and stainless as moonlight.
Reflecting upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth, for we shall take refuge in him. (8)
One was utterly devoted to Kumāra, while the other, it is said, went to Śaktidhara Kumāra.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 9 ||
It is said that in former times one [of the two] assumed the desired form of a woman, while the other remained as a man; thus did they engage in amorous sport.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 10 ||
One steals the fresh butter from the cowherd’s house, while another bestows upon the wise that supreme nectar;
reflecting on which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth, for we shall take refuge in him. (11)
For one indeed attains the reputation of being "one who possesses desire," while the other likewise attains the reputation of being "one whose desires have been destroyed."
"Or which of these two is superior? Let the elders reflect upon this and speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (12)
For one, there is the worldly rumor that he is born; for another, there is no such report of being defiled by faults.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 13 ||
One had a livelihood based on usury, while the other had a livelihood based on great fortune.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (14)
One has reached the path of the arrow, while the other today casts that very same arrow for the sake of victory over the enemy;
having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders, being truthful, declare it, and we shall take refuge in him. || 15 ||
One shines with two eyes consisting of the sun and the moon, while another has three eyes in the form of the sun, the moon, and fire.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 16 ||
One always dwells in the center of the solar orb, while the other is ever more capable of piercing through the very core of the sun.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 17 ||
One, however, set his mind upon protecting the distressed goat, while the other set his mind upon training the intoxicated elephant.
"Or which of these two is superior? Let the elders deliberate upon this and speak the truth; we shall take refuge with him. || 18 ||
Having attained the state of a cowherd, one shines forth, while another is proclaimed as the leader of the lords of bulls.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (19)
One [Viṣṇu] obtained Brahmā from his own navel-lotus, while another [Śiva] cut off Brahmā’s head with the tip of his fingernail.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 20 ||
One attains joy by dwelling in but a single part of the universe, while another gains fame as the "Lord of the Universe" (Viśveśvara).
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 21 ||
One is celebrated in the world as Keśava, while the other attains universal renown as Vyomakeśa.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 22 ||
One drew forth his own eye to fill the lotus, while the other then gave him his eye and his discus.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 23 ||
One indeed remains submerged in waters like the unfathomable, greedy ocean, while the other truly dwells upon the peak of Mount Kailāsa;
having reflected on which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth, for we shall take refuge with him. || 24 ||
One indeed performed austerities on a mountain peak for the sake of the gods, while another granted him a son, Sāmba, who was superior even to the earth.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 25 ||
One attains blueness in the body alone, while another attains blueness in the throat alone;
having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth, and we shall take refuge in him. || 26 ||
One gains fame here by committing the slaughter of a cow, while the other becomes truly famous by killing a tiger.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 27 ||
One approaches his eight queens constantly and swiftly, while the other bears the eightfold form eternally.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 28 ||
One fashions a golden garment for his waist, while another holds a golden mountain-bow at the tip of his hand;
having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth—we shall take refuge in him. (29)
One had on his head a mere peacock feather, while the other possessed the gaze of the son of the one whose vehicle is the excellent peacock.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 30 ||
One places the Kaustubha jewel upon his heart; another wears the serpent-king as a necklace, with its thousand-hooded jewels.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 31 ||
Because he is the younger brother of Indra, he is praised as Upendra; yet another is worshipped by the hosts of gods, beginning with Indra, as the one worthy of adoration.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 32 ||
One person, though possessing fortune, still desires wealth; another, even while wandering for alms, bestows good fortune upon others.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 33 ||
One held the Pāñcajanya conch in his hand here, while the other likewise held the skull of the manifold Creator.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 34 ||
One was renowned by his own name as Mādhava, while the other was indeed renowned by his own name as Umādhava.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 35 ||
One approaches the Vṛndāvana forest and wanders there with cows, while the other roams here in the cremation ground together with spirits.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 36 ||
One once performed the taking away of mere honey, while the other likewise performed the taking away of a potent poison.
"Or who among these two is superior? Let the elders reflect upon this and speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 37 ||
One is indeed skilled in the slaying of Kaiṭabha, while the other is likewise exceedingly skilled in the destruction of Death itself.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 38 ||
One produces the soft sound of a flute among the cowherd settlements; the other lets out a terrifying, boisterous laugh amidst the rhythmic cadences.
"Or which of these two is superior? Let the elders reflect upon this and speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (39)
This one is renowned as "He whose vehicle is the Lord of Birds," while the other is called "He whose vehicle is the preeminent Bull."
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 40 ||
One, indeed, is known through the sacred tradition as "born from a womb," while the other attains world-wide renown as "unborn."
"Or who among these two is superior? Let the elders reflect upon this and speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 41 ||
One is well-known throughout the world as impermanent, while the other, established by worldly consensus, is praised as permanent.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 42 ||
One is known as "bound by the mortar and pestle," while the other is known as "released from the fetters of existence."
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge with him. || 43 ||
One was treated with honor by the horses of Pārtha’s chariot, while the other had his majesty humbled in battle by Pārtha.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 44 ||
One was manifested as Janārdana, while the other was clearly praised as Śaṅkara.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 45 ||
One here has surpassed Kubera, the possessor of abundant wealth, by means of his devotion; another has been sustained by that very devotion which possesses even greater splendor.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 46 ||
One has his own wife taken away by lowly hunters and others; the other, though himself made a target by hunters, is protected on all sides by the Vedas.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 47 ||
The servants of one have their limbs severely scorched, while the servants of the other bear lines of prosperity;
reflecting upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth, for we shall take refuge with him. (48)
One has placed a white lotus as a tilaka upon his forehead, while another has placed the fire as a tilaka upon his forehead;
let the elders, having reflected on which of these two is superior, speak the truth regarding him.
We take refuge [in them]. || 49 ||
One places a garland made of *tulasī* upon his chest, while another wears a garland of skulls as prescribed by the Creator.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 50 ||
In this world, one is followed by cowherds, while another, naked as the sky, is followed by the guardians of the quarters.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 51 ||
One meets [the other] subsequently. (* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *) ||
Let the elders, having reflected upon which of these two is superior, speak the truth; we shall take refuge in that very one. || 52 ||
One wandered through the thicket, longed for by deer; the other wandered carrying a deer in the palm of his hand.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 53 ||
One had his own wife taken away by the ten-faced Rāvaṇa, while the other had half of his body occupied by the playful charms of his bride.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 54 ||
One indeed bound his quiver with masses of rocks, while another fashioned that very same quiver into the three cities.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 55 ||
One indeed burnt Laṅkā with his monkey-army, while another burnt that triple city with his hand.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 56 ||
One indeed accomplishes his own task through monkey-soldiers, while another accomplishes his own task through the hosts of the lords of the gods.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in that one. || 57 ||
One entered into the midst of the waters of the Sarayū, while the other bore the triple-pathed river (Gaṅgā) like a mere drop within his matted locks.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 58 ||
One worships Śiva in this world at Setu as Rāmeśvara; today, however, another is beheld by people.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (59)
One, having assumed the body of a fish, went into the waters of the ocean; the other is famous as the one whose banner bears the emblem of a fish.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in that very one. || 60 ||
One assumed the form of Nṛsiṃha and slew the Daitya, while another slew that very same one during his incarnation as Śarabha.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 61 ||
One was called a rogue by everyone, while the other was called a teacher of knowledge by everyone.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in that one. || 62 ||
And here, though alone, he slew Tāṭakā, who had been struck down by theft; another, however, killed the lord of the Rākṣasas, who was blinded by pride.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 63 ||
For even those who possess power...
Having reflected on which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in whichever one they name. || 64 ||

At present, one is renowned here as the great god Vāsudeva; since he has always been so celebrated, let the elders consider which of these two is superior and speak the truth—we shall take refuge in him. (65)
One suddenly pushed a cart with his foot, while another pushed a mountain with the nail of a toe.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 66 ||
One made the three worlds fit within three steps; another made the three worlds tremble by the strike of his foot.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in that one. (67)
One attains the nature of one [element], while it attains the nature of another; it attains the state of darkness (tāmasatva) and the state of goodness (sāttvikatva).
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 68 ||

One is blue, immersed in the waters of the dark Yamunā; the other is white, wearing the even whiter celestial river (Gaṅgā). Reflecting upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in that one. || 69 ||
The son of one was indeed consumed by the fire of his father's eyes, while the calf of another has truly attained eternal life;
reflecting upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth, for we shall take refuge in him.
One, assuming the form of a boar, scratched the earth; another, for the conquest of the cities, made the earth his chariot-wheel.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in that one. || 71 ||
One man was unable to restrain his own fickle wife, while another clearly divided his woman in half.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 72 ||
One shines most brilliantly with a crest of peacock feathers; another shines most brilliantly with the new moon as his crown.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (73)
For one, birth as a pig is easily obtained; for another, however, it is well known that birth in the form of a śarabha is difficult.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 74 ||
One shines intensely with a single lotus-face, while another shines with five well-known faces, O King.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (75)
One is renowned throughout the three worlds as four-armed, while the other is widely celebrated in the world with ten arms.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 76 ||
One attains the powerful strength of the five weapons, and another attains the powerful strength of all weapons.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 77 ||
One fainted from the arrow of a Kirāta in the dense forest, while the other indeed caused the Daityas stationed in the difficult-to-reach Tripura to faint;
reflecting upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth— we shall take refuge in him.
But the enemy of the cities, the universal sovereign of the gods, who bestowed the discus, having obtained that single discus, protected the worlds.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (79)
"One has three legs" is a well-known saying in the world; yet at that time, even the servant of the other was equally famous.
Having reflected on which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth, and we shall take refuge in him. (80)
One was known as Sādhu Hayavaktra, while the son of the other was known as Ibhavaktra.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 81 ||
To one, the four-faced Brahmā alone appears as a son; indeed, to another, the six-faced Kārttikeya alone appears as a son.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge with him. (82)

Having taken up the Veda, one [Brahmā] first instructed it for the sake of ritual procedure; another [Viṣṇu] established that procedure among the horses of the Vedas, and he [Śiva] composed the Sūtra.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 83 ||
One slew Naraka here most easily, while another slew many Narakas even more easily.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge with him. || 84 ||
One indeed begs for the alms of a supplicant, while another gives them; the former brings only suffering, whereas the latter brings happiness both in this world and the next.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 85 ||
One, having slain the crocodile, protected the king of elephants; the other, having slain Death, protected the son of the sage.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 86 ||
One drank the essence of breast milk with its intense flow of poison; the other drank the Kālakūṭa, which strikes terror into the world.
Let the elders reflect upon which of these two is superior and speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. (87)
One bound the ocean with a single morsel of food; another drank up the ocean with a single morsel of food.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 88 ||
One [incarnation] slew the multitude of mountains upon descending [to earth], while another, having taken his descent, received the command: "Conquer the enemies."
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; for that very purpose we have exerted ourselves. (89)
One was indeed the bringer of victory to Arjuna by virtue of being his charioteer, while the other became the bringer of victory to Arjuna through the granting of divine weapons.
"Or which of these two is superior?"—having reflected thus, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 90 ||
One pierced the excellent mountain Sumeru as if it were a blade of grass, while the other held Mount Govardhana in his hand.
Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 91 ||
Among all the gods, they say that one among the twice-born is supreme, but those who know the ultimate truth declare the Kṣatriya to be the highest.
"Having reflected upon which of these two is superior, let the elders speak the truth; we shall take refuge in him. || 92 ||
Therefore, non-duality alone is to be worshipped—immeasurable, eternal, stainless, formless, and free from conceptual construction.
We take refuge here in that Truth, which is the supreme, the beyond-supreme, the indivisible nature of consciousness, blissful, immutable, and unborn.
[This was composed by the son of the lord of sages named Śrīkānta, who is a jewel of nectar for those with a deep devotion to Rāmeśvara.]
In this world, however, considering this gradation of Hari, Hara, and Sthiti, let the wise indeed recite the Śataka more frequently. || 94 ||
[Thus ends the "Comparison of the Superiority of Hari and Hara."]
